newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine rights group asked to mediate in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Argentine rights group asked to mediate in Peru.

text.p: The Argentine human rights group Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo said on Wednesday it had accepted an offer from Peruvian guerrillas to mediate in talks over the fate of 72 hostages being held in Lima.

"The Association of Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo was asked by the commanders of the MRTA (Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement) of Peru to act as mediators in the conflict produced by the living conditions of political prisoners and the occupation of the Japanese embassy in Lima," the Mothers said.

Argentina's most famous human rights group said it would send a delegation to Lima on Friday headed by its president Hebe de Bonafini. The Mothers said they would explain more about their role in the talks at a news conference on Thursday.
There was no immediate word from the Peruvian government on whether it would accept mediation by the group.
A squad of Marxist Tupac Amaru guerrillas are holding 72 VIP hostages in the Japanese ambassador's Lima residence, after storming a diplomatic cocktail party Dec. 17.

Talks to end the crisis at a Red Cross safe house between the MRTA and the government appear to have stalled, with President Alberto Fujimori firmly rejecting the guerrillas' main demand that 400 jailed comrades be freed.
Representatives of the Vatican, the Red Cross and the Canadian government are currently serving on a commission of guarantors, set up under an agreement by both sides, to keep the talks going.

The white-scarved Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo was formed at the height of the Argentine military's brutal "Dirty War" against leftist guerrillas in the 1970s by mothers whose children had disappeared in the conflict.
